Recipes, professions, stations and deterministic results

Crafting consumes a validated recipe's resources and produces deterministic output in one durable operation. Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Cooking and Tailoring start as templates with separate profession progression and learned recipe sets.

Scope and player interaction

Crafting consumes a validated recipe's resources and produces deterministic output in one durable operation. Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Cooking and Tailoring start as templates with separate profession progression and learned recipe sets.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase13committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Closed → RecipeList → Preview → Crafting → CommitPending → Completed → Canceled → Rejected

WBP_Crafting observes results from URPGCraftingComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Recipe_IronHatchet. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
RecipeId and Version: stable recipe.* ID; ingredients/result from server catalog
IngredientRequirements: definition IDs, integer quantities and allowed substitutes only if authored
RequiredProfessionId/Level and LearnedRecipeEntitlement: durable
StationTag/ToolTag and RangeCm: validation, not merely UI decoration
CurrencyCost and BatchLimit: bounded integers
ResultDefinitionId/Quantity and FixedAffixes: deterministic initial policy
CraftActionId/CommandId: terminal receipt generates stable output instance identity

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGCraftingComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_CraftingLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
GetCraftableRecipes(StationContext) -> RecipeViews; owner-authorized read
RequestCraft(CommandId, RecipeId, BatchCount, StationContext, ExpectedInventoryRevision) -> Started|MissingMaterials|RecipeLocked
CancelCraft(ActionId) -> Canceled|AlreadyCommitted
FinalizeCraft(ActionId) -> ResultReceipt|NoSpace|Interrupted; server
LearnRecipe(CommandId, RecipeId, TrainerOffer) -> Learned|AlreadyKnown|RequirementsFailed

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. At Station_Forge the player selects IronHatchet. UI previews 4 CopperOre, 2 AshLog and 25 currency, required Blacksmithing level 1 and deterministic one-hatchet output.
  2. Server verifies interaction, learned recipe, profession/tool/station gates, batch bound and alive/action state; it starts the authored craft duration without consuming materials yet.
  3. On completion revalidate current ingredients and output capacity using one planned transaction, including space freed by consumed stacks.
  4. Backend locks character inventory/wallet/profession/recipe records, consumes exact materials/currency, creates one gear UUID, adds profession XP and receipt together.
  5. Return committed output identity and revisions. PaperZD/tool/VFX cues observe success; no animation notify calls material consumption or output grant.
  6. Disconnect immediately after confirm or commit: unresolved action cancels under policy, but committed receipt remains. On another zone login, load the one hatchet and consumed inputs without replaying the recipe.
  7. Repeat-craft requests use separate bounded commands after prior receipt or an explicitly atomic batch; never an unbounded client loop.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Create four profession definitions and station tags: Forge/Blacksmithing, AlchemyBench/Alchemy, Cookfire/Cooking, Loom/Tailoring.
  2. Author DA_Recipe_IronHatchet, DA_Recipe_HealingDraught, DA_Recipe_GrilledDace and DA_Recipe_WovenCloak with fixed outputs. Cooking input can come from the development fixture/vendor before fishing Phase 14; replace that sourcing path in the integrated loop afterward.
  3. Place BP_CraftingStation at Hearthford forge with StationId and tag; attach interaction interface only, not character inventory.
  4. Build WBP_Crafting with recipe filters, learned/locked state, ingredient counts, result tooltip, quantity and confirm/cancel. Bind counts to current inventory revision.
  5. Reopen gathering/loot/vendor catalogs so each ingredient has a real source. Add native component to authorized player command route and connect backend atomic command endpoint.
  6. Create delayed-after-commit and disconnect-before-completion service fixtures; rejoin L_Thornweald to verify exactly-one output.

Reopen Phase13 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_Rillmere / Station_Forge / Recipe_IronHatchet / Character_A. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Missing materials/profession/recipe -> explicit reason, no consumption.
Two crafts compete for same ore -> only valid serialized outcome commits; no negative materials.
Output does not fit after planned consumption -> NoSpace and no input/currency loss.
Disconnect after commit -> one output on reconnect; retry returns same UUID.
Unknown recipe version -> StaleRecipe; require refreshed preview/confirmation.
Batch=0, negative or over limit -> InvalidQuantity; no loop or overflow.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

IronHatchet example costs/yield and 4-second craft duration are tuning proposals. Initial success is deterministic; quality/failure rolls are disabled until audit/balance rules are approved.

Ledger links recipe version, consumed stacks, output UUID and profession XP. Craft UI supports controller quantity changes and text ingredient deficits. Track material sinks, output volume and disconnect reconciliation.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
